We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline (para? Actually the amide attaches to aniline). The target has two aromatic rings: ring A (tolyl) attached to sulfonyl group (SO2) attached to ring B (phenyl) which is para-substituted with the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain (C=C-CO-NH-aniline). The aniline is attached to the amide nitrogen (N attached to phenyl). So overall three fragments: (1) p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride precursor for sulfonamide formation; (2) the α,β-unsaturated acid precursor for amide formation; (3) aniline as amine.

We need 3 reactions: likely step 1: formation of amide (carboxylic acid to amide) between cinnamic acid derivative and aniline. Step 2: Doebner modification to make the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. Step 3: sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and phenyl sulfonamide (the phenyl sulfonyl attached to ring B). Actually sulfonamide formation attaches sulfonyl chloride to amine; we have sulfonamide linking p-tolyl sulfonyl to phenyl ring B (the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to phenyl B). So we need p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and phenyl amine (the phenyl B with amine). But phenyl B already has amine? In target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to phenyl B (the ring bearing the unsaturated amide). So the phenyl B must have an amine (NH) that reacts with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide. So we need phenyl B with NH2 (i.e., aniline) as precursor. However phenyl B also has the unsaturated amide side chain attached to the same nitrogen? Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to phenyl B (the ring). The amide nitrogen is attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). That's a separate aniline attached to the amide carbonyl. So phenyl B has a sulfonamide nitrogen attached to it (i.e., -SO2-NH-Ph). The amide side chain attaches to the phenyl B via a carbon chain (C=C-CO-NH-aniline). So phenyl B has two substituents: sulfonamide nitrogen (attached via N) and the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain attached via carbon at para position? Actually the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(...). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl B (the sulfonyl attached to phenyl B). So phenyl B is attached to sulfonyl via N (i.e., -SO2-N-Ph). The phenyl B also has the side chain at para position relative to N? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches to the sulfonyl group, which attaches to phenyl B at position 1 (the sulfonyl attached to phenyl). The side chain is at para position (maybe). So phenyl B is a phenyl with two substituents: sulfonamide (via N) and the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain (via carbon). So we need to construct phenyl B with those substituents.

Retrosynthesis: Step 1 (most recent) could be sulfonamide formation: combine p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (or p-tolyl sulfonyl fluoride) with phenyl B amine (which is an aniline bearing the side chain). That gives the sulfonamide linking the two rings.

Thus precursor 1: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH3). Precursor 2: phenyl B amine (i.e., 4-(C=C-CO-NH-aniline)aniline). That amine is an aniline with the side chain attached at para position.

Step 2: formation of amide between cinnamic acid derivative (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The amide carbonyl attaches to the aniline nitrogen. So we need the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) and aniline.

Thus precursor for phenyl B amine: we need aniline (c3ccccc3N) as separate component, and the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) to form amide. The amide product is the side chain attached to phenyl B via carbon (C=C-CO-NH-aniline). Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to aniline, not to phenyl B. So the phenyl B amine is not the aniline; the phenyl B is the aromatic ring bearing the side chain; the side chain includes the amide linking to aniline. So phenyl B amine is not needed; phenyl B is a phenyl with a side chain that includes an amide to aniline. So the amide formation step is between cinnamic acid (or its derivative) and aniline to give the side chain (C=C-CO-NH-aniline). That product is attached to phenyl B via the carbon of the side chain (the α,β-unsaturated acid attaches at its α carbon to phenyl B). Actually the side chain is attached to phenyl B via the carbon of the double bond (the β carbon?). The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So phenyl B has a substituent: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH (aniline). So the side chain is attached via the carbon of the double bond (the β carbon) to phenyl B. So the α,β-unsaturated acid is derived from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl B) via Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative). Then amide formation attaches aniline to the acid carbonyl.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

1. Sulfonamide formation: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + phenyl B amine (which is the phenyl B bearing the side chain and an NH group? Wait phenyl B amine is the phenyl B with the side chain attached, and the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to phenyl B via N (i.e., phenyl B is attached to sulfonyl via N). So phenyl B must have an amine group (NH) to react with sulfonyl chloride. Indeed the SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2... indicates the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the sulfonyl group and to phenyl B (i.e., -SO2-NH-Ph). So phenyl B must have an NH (aniline) that is free (not part of the side chain). But the phenyl B also has the side chain at para position. So phenyl B is 4-(C=C-CO-NH-aniline)aniline (i.e., 4-aminophenyl with side chain). So the amine on phenyl B is the sulfonamide nitrogen (the same N). So phenyl B amine is the aniline that will be sulfonylated.

Thus step 1: sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and 4-(C=C-CO-NH-aniline)aniline (i.e., 4-aminophenyl with side chain). That yields the target.

Step 2: amide formation between cinnamic acid (or its unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The product is 4-(C=C-CO-NH-aniline)aniline? Wait the amide attaches to aniline, giving the side chain: C=C-CO-NH-aniline. The other end of the side chain attaches to phenyl B via the carbon of the double bond (the β carbon). So the phenyl B is the aromatic aldehyde used in Doebner to generate the α,β-unsaturated acid. So step 2 is amide formation: cinnamic acid (or its unsaturated acid) + aniline -> α,β-unsaturated amide (C=C-CO-NH-aniline). This product is attached to phenyl B? Actually the product of amide formation is the side chain attached to aniline, not attached to phenyl B. The phenyl B is separate; we need to attach the side chain to phenyl B via a carbon-carbon bond (the double bond). That bond is formed in Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid). So step 3 (or step 2) is Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde (4-aminobenzaldehyde) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) with the amine still present (para-aminocinnamic acid). Then step 2 amide formation attaches aniline to the acid carbonyl, giving the side chain attached to phenyl B (which still has the amine). Then step 1 sulfonamide formation attaches p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride to that amine, giving final product.

Thus three steps: (a) Doebner modification to make 4-aminocinnamic acid from 4-aminobenzaldehyde and malonic acid. (b) Amide coupling of that acid with aniline to give 4-(C=C-CO-NH-aniline)aniline. (c) Sulfonamide formation with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride to give final target.

Now we need to find template IDs for each reaction. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria for each transformation.

First, Doebner modification: functional groups broken: aromatic aldehyde, carboxylic acid (malonic acid) maybe? Actually malonic acid is broken (one CO2 lost). Functional groups formed: C-C double bond (alkene). So we can search with functional_groups_broken: ["aldehydes", "carboxylic acids"] and functional_groups_formed: ["C-C double bonds"].
